messages.subject: portable (?) C++ threading???
parts:
We need to start thinking about how to run
multi-threading.

The design of the auto-dif will work in multiple
threads if the two memory management variables
in stan::agrad are made thread local.

The design of the models is thread safe, so
a single model populated with data on construction
can be used safely across multiple threads.

The alternatives I see right away are to:

1. Use g++ thread local variables. I think
it works on all the g++ compilers we're using.

2. Boost threads. They have thread local vars
that are more cross-platform. But it's not a header-only
library and I'm far from earning my merit badge
in C++ builds.

3. Rethink how auto-dif allocations memory to
make it thread safe. One crazy idea I had was
to add an integer template variable to stan::agrad::var
for thread ID, as in:

var<1> x = 4.0;

to create an auto-dif variable in thread 1's memory
space. We could default the parameter to 1 and it'd
work just fine. This wouldn't require any synch at
all and would probably be faster, but then we'd have
to duplicate all the code on a per-thread basis and
pass this templating right up through the model. So
we couldn't do sharing of data any more.

4. Another alternative would be to add a pointer to
memory as part of var or vari. Then the very first
vari need to be handled, but any subsequent expressions
require no synch. I think one of the other AD packages
does things this way (CppAD, I think).

Any thoughts or suggestions on how we should go
about this?

- Bob
